quality.review_scope: All four supplied main pages read and visually inspected, with independent source, canonical, molecular, apparatus and reader audits. Three CdS/HgS/CdS architectures retain distinct exchange/deposition sequences and source-assigned optical contexts. Counterions, several feed doses and the core-size discrepancy remain unresolved. Matching SI not located or verified; cited upstream preparations and theory are not independently reviewed here.
missing_fields: Cd and Hg precursor salts/counterions, hexametaphosphate counterion and dose, preparation of H2S/water stock, and pH-adjustment reagents are not reported.
No current-paper TEM micrograph, XRD/SAED pattern, refined phase, unit cell or atomic-coordinate file. Figure 1 is a schematic and cites earlier theory/morphology.

Synthesis temperature, detailed growth timing, final workup/isolation, yield and physical-batch identifiers are not supplied. Room temperature is stated for optical experiments, not assigned numerically or silently transferred to synthesis.
conflicts: Step A says CdS grows to 3.5 nm; the later system descriptions and Figure 1 say 3.2 nm for all three cores.
Figure 4 inset uses bleach labels for representative traces; discussion assigns the low-energy long-lived component to stimulated emission.

quality.review_scope: All four supplied main pages read and visually inspected, with independent source, canonical, molecular, apparatus and reader audits. Three CdS/HgS/CdS architectures retain distinct exchange/deposition sequences and source-assigned optical contexts. Counterions, several feed doses and the core-size discrepancy remain unresolved. Matching SI not located or verified; cited upstream preparations and theory are not independently reviewed here.
missing_fields: Cd and Hg precursor salts/counterions, hexametaphosphate counterion and dose, preparation of H2S/water stock, and pH-adjustment reagents are not reported.
No current-paper TEM micrograph, XRD/SAED pattern, refined phase, unit cell or atomic-coordinate file. Figure 1 is a schematic and cites earlier theory/morphology.

Synthesis temperature, detailed growth timing, final workup/isolation, yield and physical-batch identifiers are not supplied. Room temperature is stated for optical experiments, not assigned numerically or silently transferred to synthesis.
conflicts: Step A says CdS grows to 3.5 nm; the later system descriptions and Figure 1 say 3.2 nm for all three cores.
Figure 4 inset uses bleach labels for representative traces; discussion assigns the low-energy long-lived component to stimulated emission.

Three CdS/HgS/CdS architectures retain distinct exchange/deposition sequences and source-assigned optical contexts. Counterions, several feed doses and the core-size discrepancy remain unresolved. missing_fields: Cd and Hg precursor salts/counterions, hexametaphosphate counterion and dose, preparation of H2S/water stock, and pH-adjustment reagents are not reported.
No current-paper TEM micrograph, XRD/SAED pattern, refined phase, unit cell or atomic-coordinate file. Figure 1 is a schematic and cites earlier theory/morphology.

Synthesis temperature, detailed growth timing, final workup/isolation, yield and physical-batch identifiers are not supplied. Room temperature is stated for optical experiments, not assigned numerically or silently transferred to synthesis.
No separate Figure 2 spectrum for the intermediate two-CdS-layer overcoat; the shown sequence proceeds from one to three layers.
conflicts: Step A says CdS grows to 3.5 nm; the later system descriptions and Figure 1 say 3.2 nm for all three cores.
Figure 4 inset uses bleach labels for representative traces; discussion assigns the low-energy long-lived component to stimulated emission.

Six annealing variants, common glass preparation, optical and AFM specimens, and author calculations retain their own evidence scopes. Glass proportions, sulfur reagent, literal vessel identity and size/radius ambiguity remain unresolved. Matching SI not located or verified; cited external works not independently inspected.
missing_fields: Mixture proportions, absolute charges, sulfur chemical source/loading and addition timing, quantitative purity grades, annealing atmosphere and temperature ramps are not reported.
No current TEM, XRD, SAED, refined atomic lattice, crystal coordinate file, yield, error bars or raw numerical spectra are supplied.
The source alternates between generic QD size, calculated radius and AFM grain height. No universal diameter conversion is justified.
Precursor-selection supervision is partial: printed PbO2 is known but the sulfur precursor identity is absent. No complete precursor set or executable weighed recipe is claimed.

value.value:
Refinement of F^2^ against ALL reflections.  The weighted R-factor wR and 
 goodness of fit S are based on F^2^, conventional R-factors R are based 
 on F, with F set to zero for negative F^2^. The threshold expression of 
 F^2^ > 2sigma(F^2^) is used only for calculating R-factors(gt) etc. and is 
 not relevant to the choice of reflections for refinement.  R-factors based 
 on F^2^ are statistically about twice as large as those based on F, and R- 
 factors based on ALL data will be even larger.

 treatment of cell esds is used for estimating esds involving l.s. planes.

operations.description: Supply sulfur for thirteen layers at the beginning; add Cd layerwise with four-hour intervals. Charge sulfur sufficient for thirteen monolayers at the start, then add only Cd precursor one monolayer at a time with four-hour intervals. This is a distinct modified SILAR schedule. Turbidity begins at seven layers but remains approximately constant and smaller rather than cycling. QY is low, particles are rods, and XRD gives wurtzite:zinc-blende 40:60. Missing fields: complete initial formulation, exact aliquots.

value.value: A 7 nm CdSe core-only sample has about 15% ensemble QY at 680 nm before washing. Washing makes it essentially nonemissive; even the diluted unwashed sample is not visible at single-dot level on a slide. Its synthesis method is not reported and must not be borrowed from the 5.5 nm procedure.

operations.description: Acquire TCSPC, fit triexponentials and report mean lifetime. Use PicoQuant LDH-P-C-405B pulsed excitation, wide-field illumination and neutral-density attenuation. The stated optical-power regime is several nW to hundreds of pW, not exact interval endpoints. Collect through a 100×, NA 1.3 oil-immersion objective, dichroic and long-pass filter; use Perkin-Elmer SPCM-AQR-14 SPAD and PicoQuant PicoHarp 300 TCSPC. Igor Pro fits triexponential histograms and computes the reported average lifetime from amplitude and lifetime coefficients. The eighteen rows report mean fit coefficients and mean average lifetimes for four core sizes. Amplitude coefficients are normalized, but displayed rounding and averaging need not reproduce exact unity or exact average lifetime from the printed mean coefficients. Initial guesses strongly affect individual components, less the converged mean lifetime. Missing fields: raw fit files.

operations.description: Illuminate continuously and acquire CCD time series. A Coherent Cube continuous-wave diode at 405 nm illuminates the sample. A simple lens gives an approximately circular focal spot. PL passes through a dichroic and spectral filter to a liquid-nitrogen-cooled Princeton Spec-10 CCD. Collect 20,000 frames with 100 ms integration and approximately 90 ms readout while constantly illuminated, giving slightly more than one hour total. SI S8 reports readout as 91 ms. Missing fields: exact power per specimen.

operations.description: Classify each dot/frame against background threshold and use ever-emitting population. Igor Pro groups pixels into dots, averages pixel intensity per dot and frame, and applies I_pix > BG + 2 sqrt(BG). I_pix is not background-subtracted. Below-threshold dots may remain discernible. Statistics use all dots that ever emitted, not every physical deposited particle. Main prose uses greater than 99% on-time over sixty minutes, while Figure 3 uses at least 99%. Retain the printed inequality distinction; denominator is dots that emitted at least once during observation. Missing fields: raw trajectories.

operations.description: Compare ODE/OD primary-amine shell conditions and optional late OD dilution. For 3–4 nm cores in ODE/primary amine, precipitation begins after about seven monolayers following Cd addition. Added S/ODE initially redissolves particles; at more than eleven layers an entire sulfur aliquot no longer fully clears the solution. Replacing ODE by OD delays initial turbidity until at least eleven monolayers. Beginning at ten monolayers, modest OD dilution reduces dot concentration and improves size/shape uniformity. Combined with longer annealing, this produces the Table 2 row 3 spherical/faceted population; no complete per-layer dilution schedule is given. Missing fields: complete per-row protocol. This operation groups source-described alternatives for navigation, not a single physical charge containing all alternatives simultaneously.

operations.description: Compare primary, secondary and no-added-amine preparations. The described typical shell reaction adds all primary oleylamine initially, while OA enters with each Cd aliquot. An illustrative fourteen-layer context compares 15 mmol amine with 6.5 mmol OA. The medium is approximately equal polar/nonpolar mass; this is not a complete formulation recipe. Dioctylamine suppresses precipitation but gives nonemissive octahedral particles with predominantly wurtzite phase. The proposed eight alternating polar facets and nonpolar overall shape are the authors’ interpretation, not an atomic-coordinate reconstruction. Removing added amine, while allowing residual core-bound primary amine, causes the earliest precipitation from three monolayers. Table 2 separately places hexagonal faceting beyond six monolayers. Missing fields: exact secondary-amine amount, all row batch labels. This operation groups source-described alternatives for navigation, not a single physical charge containing all alternatives simultaneously.

Do not replace the experimental paragraph’s switch wording with a single exact cycle. Missing fields: exact switch cycle. This operation groups source-described alternatives for navigation, not a single physical charge containing all alternatives simultaneously.

value.value: Withdraw 1% or 10% after each complete shell cycle but retain the original precursor doses. Both reduce precipitation; the larger withdrawal almost eliminates it but gives poor QY and misshapen particles. Lesser withdrawal gives rods or irregular particles.

quality.review_scope: All 2 supplied main pages and 3 content-matched SI pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source extraction and canonical scientific audits passed. Source conflicts and unreported parameters are preserved. This scope does not establish identical physical aliquots across analytical techniques or measured atomic coordinates.
missing_fields: No atomic coordinates, CIF, unit-cell constants, occupancy refinement, interface lattice mapping or crystallographic atom model is supplied. SAED establishes author phase assignments only.
No XRD pattern, Raman spectrum, electrical transport or elemental spatial map is supplied. XRF must not be relabeled XRD or EDS.

Samples are explicitly labeled 1–4 and figures identify those stages. Exact batch/aliquot provenance, microscopy transfer/isolation details, and whether TEM, SAED, magnetometry and optical measurements used the same physical batch are unreported.
Reaction vessel, heating apparatus, numeric inert pressure, gas identity, ramp rates and stirring speeds are not reported. Dioctyl-ether boiling point is not numerically supplied.

CdCl2 hydration and 80.5% assay basis are unresolved. Recrystallization solvent ratio/amount/temperature, vacuum pressure and drying duration are absent. Purity and hydration of isolated Cd(acac)2 are not analytically quantified.
Centrifugation force/speed/time, yield or final mass of 4, final particle concentration and nitrogen storage temperature/duration are absent.
Instrument models, TEM voltage, XRF source/substrate/calibration, magnetic sample mass/state, full FC/ZFC protocol, SI-3 field, optical concentration and fluorescence correction details are absent.

Core–shell intermediates and dewetting mechanism remain author-supported interpretations with an isolation limitation; no separately varied annealing study, in situ kinetics or interface thermodynamic parameters are supplied.
No synthesis replicate count, error bars, numerical dispersity, failed-isolation trial count or raw data files are provided in the supplied bundle.
conflicts: SI inset mol% values Fe 0.0562, Pt 0.0604, Cd 1.5447, S 1.9262 do not directly reproduce the main stated approximate Fe/Pt/Cd/S ratio 1:1:3:3.6. Corrections, substrate contribution and quantification basis are not supplied. Preserve both representations; do not silently rescale either.

structure_assets.description: Curator reconstruction from the adopted Table 2 average structure: mixed Si/Al sites, fractional indium occupancies and alternative InII/InIIa positions. Geometry/occupancy only; ADPs omitted. Nominal Si100Al92 differs from average Si96Al96. Not an author-supplied CIF, unique ordered specimen, full refinement or DFT-ready input.

quality.review_scope: Complete supplied 9-page main article and matched 14-page SI reviewed. Separate independent source, canonical/reader, reflection-table and molecular-binding audits passed. One synthesis route, three acquisition procedures and six analytical/model contexts retain their own sample identities. Average position/occupancy reconstruction is qualified separately; condition conflicts, two uncertain SI signs and unresolved physical sample links remain explicit. No exact ordered structure or training task is admitted.
missing_fields: The prose and Table 1 disagree on dehydration temperatures/durations and indium-contact duration. Neither version is selected as a resolved recipe.
Absolute host and indium amounts, capillary dimensions, feed-flow rate, indium/crystal temperature difference, redox vacuum, gas amount/flow, final vacuum and cooling rate are unreported.
Nominal Si100Al92 differs from the averaged Table 2 model containing 96 Si and 96 Al; fixed and varied occupancies are refinement parameters.
Average disorder, fractional site populations and charge-compensation hypotheses do not specify a unique atomistic specimen or a DFT-ready structure.

A curator reconstruction of the reported average positions and occupancies is qualified for source interpretation. It omits unresolved ADPs, preserves mixed and alternative sites, and is not a full refinement, ordered DFT model or exact-structure training label. Two SI signs remain unresolved.
The approximately 4300 Å XPS depth statement cannot be reconstructed from the displayed approximately 10 s sputter cycles and reported rate.
The input Na-X synthesis and cited control preparations are external references, not complete procedures supplied here.
conflicts: Experimental prose: initial/redehydration623K48h1e-6Torr; In contact623K96 h. Table 1: dehydrations673K3 days; In contact623K5 days. Unresolved same-study conflicts, not approved alternative protocols.
Table 2 footnotec models96Si+96Al, while nominal In66Si100Al92O384 framework and text use100Si92Al. Preserve refinement representation and nominal composition separately.

Cluster charge7+ and local In1.75+/ca2+ are proposed; total83+versusframework92- motivates unverified oxygen-loss4.5/unitcell or9H+/unitcell alternatives. Never add those atoms/defects to measured coordinate model.
Figure 1B In87-X spectrum copied fromreference 34. Figure 2A Inmetal intensity scaled percaption1/20. ProductXPS versus reactant/reference must remain separate.
Figure 3 caption says0.6Å/s and~10 s sputtering after each measurement, while prose says depth~4300Å. Printed depth not derivable from shown20-ishcycles; do not invent total sputtering schedule.
Table 1 data/parameter ratios17.1/18.3 correspond observed reflections754/44 and1207/66, although heading labelsm/s withm=allunique1209/2032. Preserve printed table and flag definition mismatch.
Heo subsectionc heading sayssitesIprimeandIIprime but body/finaltable placesInIIa atsiteII; use exactatomlabels and preserve heading discrepancy.

structure_assets.description: Curator reconstruction from the adopted Table 2 average structure: mixed Si/Al sites, fractional indium occupancies and alternative InII/InIIa positions. Geometry/occupancy only; ADPs omitted. Nominal Si100Al92 differs from average Si96Al96. Not an author-supplied CIF, unique ordered specimen, full refinement or DFT-ready input.

quality.review_scope: Complete supplied 9-page main article and matched 14-page SI reviewed. Separate independent source, canonical/reader, reflection-table and molecular-binding audits passed. One synthesis route, three acquisition procedures and six analytical/model contexts retain their own sample identities. Average position/occupancy reconstruction is qualified separately; condition conflicts, two uncertain SI signs and unresolved physical sample links remain explicit. No exact ordered structure or training task is admitted.
missing_fields: The prose and Table 1 disagree on dehydration temperatures/durations and indium-contact duration. Neither version is selected as a resolved recipe.
Absolute host and indium amounts, capillary dimensions, feed-flow rate, indium/crystal temperature difference, redox vacuum, gas amount/flow, final vacuum and cooling rate are unreported.
Nominal Si100Al92 differs from the averaged Table 2 model containing 96 Si and 96 Al; fixed and varied occupancies are refinement parameters.
Average disorder, fractional site populations and charge-compensation hypotheses do not specify a unique atomistic specimen or a DFT-ready structure.

A curator reconstruction of the reported average positions and occupancies is qualified for source interpretation. It omits unresolved ADPs, preserves mixed and alternative sites, and is not a full refinement, ordered DFT model or exact-structure training label. Two SI signs remain unresolved.
The approximately 4300 Å XPS depth statement cannot be reconstructed from the displayed approximately 10 s sputter cycles and reported rate.
The input Na-X synthesis and cited control preparations are external references, not complete procedures supplied here.
conflicts: Experimental prose: initial/redehydration623K48h1e-6Torr; In contact623K96 h. Table 1: dehydrations673K3 days; In contact623K5 days. Unresolved same-study conflicts, not approved alternative protocols.
Table 2 footnotec models96Si+96Al, while nominal In66Si100Al92O384 framework and text use100Si92Al. Preserve refinement representation and nominal composition separately.

Cluster charge7+ and local In1.75+/ca2+ are proposed; total83+versusframework92- motivates unverified oxygen-loss4.5/unitcell or9H+/unitcell alternatives. Never add those atoms/defects to measured coordinate model.
Figure 1B In87-X spectrum copied fromreference 34. Figure 2A Inmetal intensity scaled percaption1/20. ProductXPS versus reactant/reference must remain separate.
Figure 3 caption says0.6Å/s and~10 s sputtering after each measurement, while prose says depth~4300Å. Printed depth not derivable from shown20-ishcycles; do not invent total sputtering schedule.
Table 1 data/parameter ratios17.1/18.3 correspond observed reflections754/44 and1207/66, although heading labelsm/s withm=allunique1209/2032. Preserve printed table and flag definition mismatch.
Heo subsectionc heading sayssitesIprimeandIIprime but body/finaltable placesInIIa atsiteII; use exactatomlabels and preserve heading discrepancy.

quality.review_scope: Complete supplied 9-page main article and matched 14-page SI reviewed. Separate independent source, canonical/reader, reflection-table and molecular-binding audits passed. One synthesis route, three acquisition procedures and six analytical/model contexts retain their own sample identities. Average position/occupancy reconstruction is qualified separately; condition conflicts, two uncertain SI signs and unresolved physical sample links remain explicit. No exact ordered structure or training task is admitted.
missing_fields: The prose and Table 1 disagree on dehydration temperatures/durations and indium-contact duration. Neither version is selected as a resolved recipe.
Absolute host and indium amounts, capillary dimensions, feed-flow rate, indium/crystal temperature difference, redox vacuum, gas amount/flow, final vacuum and cooling rate are unreported.
Nominal Si100Al92 differs from the averaged Table 2 model containing 96 Si and 96 Al; fixed and varied occupancies are refinement parameters.
Average disorder, fractional site populations and charge-compensation hypotheses do not specify a unique atomistic specimen or a DFT-ready structure.

A curator reconstruction of the reported average positions and occupancies is qualified for source interpretation. It omits unresolved ADPs, preserves mixed and alternative sites, and is not a full refinement, ordered DFT model or exact-structure training label. Two SI signs remain unresolved.
The approximately 4300 Å XPS depth statement cannot be reconstructed from the displayed approximately 10 s sputter cycles and reported rate.
The input Na-X synthesis and cited control preparations are external references, not complete procedures supplied here.
conflicts: Experimental prose: initial/redehydration623K48h1e-6Torr; In contact623K96 h. Table 1: dehydrations673K3 days; In contact623K5 days. Unresolved same-study conflicts, not approved alternative protocols.
Table 2 footnotec models96Si+96Al, while nominal In66Si100Al92O384 framework and text use100Si92Al. Preserve refinement representation and nominal composition separately.

Cluster charge7+ and local In1.75+/ca2+ are proposed; total83+versusframework92- motivates unverified oxygen-loss4.5/unitcell or9H+/unitcell alternatives. Never add those atoms/defects to measured coordinate model.
Figure 1B In87-X spectrum copied fromreference 34. Figure 2A Inmetal intensity scaled percaption1/20. ProductXPS versus reactant/reference must remain separate.
Figure 3 caption says0.6Å/s and~10 s sputtering after each measurement, while prose says depth~4300Å. Printed depth not derivable from shown20-ishcycles; do not invent total sputtering schedule.
Table 1 data/parameter ratios17.1/18.3 correspond observed reflections754/44 and1207/66, although heading labelsm/s withm=allunique1209/2032. Preserve printed table and flag definition mismatch.
Heo subsectionc heading sayssitesIprimeandIIprime but body/finaltable placesInIIa atsiteII; use exactatomlabels and preserve heading discrepancy.

quality.review_scope: Complete supplied 9-page main article and matched 14-page SI reviewed. Separate independent source, canonical/reader, reflection-table and molecular-binding audits passed. One synthesis route, three acquisition procedures and six analytical/model contexts retain their own sample identities. Average position/occupancy reconstruction is qualified separately; condition conflicts, two uncertain SI signs and unresolved physical sample links remain explicit. No exact ordered structure or training task is admitted.
missing_fields: The prose and Table 1 disagree on dehydration temperatures/durations and indium-contact duration. Neither version is selected as a resolved recipe.
Absolute host and indium amounts, capillary dimensions, feed-flow rate, indium/crystal temperature difference, redox vacuum, gas amount/flow, final vacuum and cooling rate are unreported.
Nominal Si100Al92 differs from the averaged Table 2 model containing 96 Si and 96 Al; fixed and varied occupancies are refinement parameters.
Average disorder, fractional site populations and charge-compensation hypotheses do not specify a unique atomistic specimen or a DFT-ready structure.

A curator reconstruction of the reported average positions and occupancies is qualified for source interpretation. It omits unresolved ADPs, preserves mixed and alternative sites, and is not a full refinement, ordered DFT model or exact-structure training label. Two SI signs remain unresolved.
The approximately 4300 Å XPS depth statement cannot be reconstructed from the displayed approximately 10 s sputter cycles and reported rate.
The input Na-X synthesis and cited control preparations are external references, not complete procedures supplied here.
conflicts: Experimental prose: initial/redehydration623K48h1e-6Torr; In contact623K96 h. Table 1: dehydrations673K3 days; In contact623K5 days. Unresolved same-study conflicts, not approved alternative protocols.
Table 2 footnotec models96Si+96Al, while nominal In66Si100Al92O384 framework and text use100Si92Al. Preserve refinement representation and nominal composition separately.

Cluster charge7+ and local In1.75+/ca2+ are proposed; total83+versusframework92- motivates unverified oxygen-loss4.5/unitcell or9H+/unitcell alternatives. Never add those atoms/defects to measured coordinate model.
Figure 1B In87-X spectrum copied fromreference 34. Figure 2A Inmetal intensity scaled percaption1/20. ProductXPS versus reactant/reference must remain separate.
Figure 3 caption says0.6Å/s and~10 s sputtering after each measurement, while prose says depth~4300Å. Printed depth not derivable from shown20-ishcycles; do not invent total sputtering schedule.
Table 1 data/parameter ratios17.1/18.3 correspond observed reflections754/44 and1207/66, although heading labelsm/s withm=allunique1209/2032. Preserve printed table and flag definition mismatch.
Heo subsectionc heading sayssitesIprimeandIIprime but body/finaltable placesInIIa atsiteII; use exactatomlabels and preserve heading discrepancy.

quality.review_scope: Complete supplied 9-page main article and matched 14-page SI reviewed. Separate independent source, canonical/reader, reflection-table and molecular-binding audits passed. One synthesis route, three acquisition procedures and six analytical/model contexts retain their own sample identities. Average position/occupancy reconstruction is qualified separately; condition conflicts, two uncertain SI signs and unresolved physical sample links remain explicit. No exact ordered structure or training task is admitted.
missing_fields: The prose and Table 1 disagree on dehydration temperatures/durations and indium-contact duration. Neither version is selected as a resolved recipe.
Absolute host and indium amounts, capillary dimensions, feed-flow rate, indium/crystal temperature difference, redox vacuum, gas amount/flow, final vacuum and cooling rate are unreported.

quality.review_scope: Complete supplied 9-page main article and matched 14-page SI reviewed. Separate independent source, canonical/reader, reflection-table and molecular-binding audits passed. One synthesis route, three acquisition procedures and six analytical/model contexts retain their own sample identities. Average position/occupancy reconstruction is qualified separately; condition conflicts, two uncertain SI signs and unresolved physical sample links remain explicit. No exact ordered structure or training task is admitted.
missing_fields: The prose and Table 1 disagree on dehydration temperatures/durations and indium-contact duration. Neither version is selected as a resolved recipe.
Absolute host and indium amounts, capillary dimensions, feed-flow rate, indium/crystal temperature difference, redox vacuum, gas amount/flow, final vacuum and cooling rate are unreported.
Nominal Si100Al92 differs from the averaged Table 2 model containing 96 Si and 96 Al; fixed and varied occupancies are refinement parameters.
Average disorder, fractional site populations and charge-compensation hypotheses do not specify a unique atomistic specimen or a DFT-ready structure.

A curator reconstruction of the reported average positions and occupancies is qualified for source interpretation. It omits unresolved ADPs, preserves mixed and alternative sites, and is not a full refinement, ordered DFT model or exact-structure training label. Two SI signs remain unresolved.
The approximately 4300 Å XPS depth statement cannot be reconstructed from the displayed approximately 10 s sputter cycles and reported rate.
The input Na-X synthesis and cited control preparations are external references, not complete procedures supplied here.
conflicts: Experimental prose: initial/redehydration623K48h1e-6Torr; In contact623K96 h. Table 1: dehydrations673K3 days; In contact623K5 days. Unresolved same-study conflicts, not approved alternative protocols.
Table 2 footnotec models96Si+96Al, while nominal In66Si100Al92O384 framework and text use100Si92Al. Preserve refinement representation and nominal composition separately.

Cluster charge7+ and local In1.75+/ca2+ are proposed; total83+versusframework92- motivates unverified oxygen-loss4.5/unitcell or9H+/unitcell alternatives. Never add those atoms/defects to measured coordinate model.
Figure 1B In87-X spectrum copied fromreference 34. Figure 2A Inmetal intensity scaled percaption1/20. ProductXPS versus reactant/reference must remain separate.
Figure 3 caption says0.6Å/s and~10 s sputtering after each measurement, while prose says depth~4300Å. Printed depth not derivable from shown20-ishcycles; do not invent total sputtering schedule.
Table 1 data/parameter ratios17.1/18.3 correspond observed reflections754/44 and1207/66, although heading labelsm/s withm=allunique1209/2032. Preserve printed table and flag definition mismatch.
Heo subsectionc heading sayssitesIprimeandIIprime but body/finaltable placesInIIa atsiteII; use exactatomlabels and preserve heading discrepancy.

operations.description: Cool aerosol, pass first through EG prebubbler, then through silanized coarse-glass frit into the EG collection bubbler. Collect both dispersions without conflating them into a single measured batch. Prebubbler is before frit, although paragraph initially introduces the frit first. 2–3 cm3 EG loss in prebubbler per 24 h is an operational observation, not synthesis duration. About two-thirds of collected crystallites appear in second bubbler; one-third Si capture is a separate source-derived mass-efficiency estimate.  Frit pretreatment uses printed SiH2Cl2 in toluene; amount, concentration, treatment duration and wash/dry details are unreported. This upstream treatment is not a simultaneous gas feed.

quality.review_scope: Complete supplied 10-page main article and matched 17-page SI read and independently audited. Separate canonical/reader, molecular and apparatus audits passed. Two shell-growth routes, eight supporting procedures and eight observation contexts remain distinct. Printed conflicts and unresolved specimen joins are preserved. Precursor crystal coordinates are not CdSe/CdS product coordinates. No new training task or exact structure–recipe pair is admitted.
missing_fields: No complete executable laboratory SOP is asserted.
Upstream NH4PTC and starting CdSe-belt preparations are cited rather than supplied in full.
No supplied CdSe/CdS product atomic coordinates; precursor crystal tables do not establish a product structure.
Physical batch identity is not inferred across TEM, XRD, elemental and optical contexts.

quality.review_scope: All five supplied main pages and all three content-matched SI pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source, canonical, reader, apparatus, component and product-context audits passed. Four source ambiguities, the incomplete biotin variant and all missing quantities remain explicit. The abstract size summary and optical-model size do not establish a TEM/XRD/biotin recipe-to-specimen join. No measured atomic coordinates are supplied.
missing_fields: G1 (pdp-preparation/acetal-block-polymer): Separate initiator reagent charges, EO-stage temperature, atmosphere, addition rates, PAMA protonating reagent, precipitation/extraction volumes and durations, yields/drying/storage. Present paper has an operational summary, not a fully reproducible upstream polymer SOP. References14a/14b are cited but their full texts were not inspected.

G2 (aldehyde-polymer/biotin-polymer): Polymer/solvent charges, neutralization endpoint, biocytin-hydrazide and NaBH4 amounts, reduction duration/temperature, exact purified biotin-polymer concentration and biotin functionality. Do not infer stoichiometry, quantitative biotin coverage, reduction conditions or yield.

G3 (all dialysis operations): Membrane/MWCO, time, water-exchange schedule, temperature, final volume/concentration, recovered yield and storage. Final material is an incompletely specified dialyzed dispersion; no invented isolated powder preparation.

G4 (CdS coprecipitation): CdCl2/Na2S solution-addition volumes and unequivocal stock-versus-final concentration basis, hydration state, pH, numerical ambient temperature, atmosphere, speed and addition rates. Do not multiply2.5mM by8mL to assert an added reagent charge or total yield;8mL is the initial polymer-solution volume.

G5 (comparison and concentration variants): Independent whole-batch records, exact workup and specimen links, replicate counts and outcomes per salt/concentration combination. Variants/photographs are not verified independent experiments or a timing sequence.

G6 (optical/structural sample links): Which Figure2 concentration supplies absorption trace d, Figure3 specimen, SI TEM or SI XRD; whether SI samples are biotin-ended. No exact recipe-to-structure, biotin-to-TEM, or structure-to-FRET join. Nominal same material is insufficient.

G7 (size and atomistic structure): TEM particle counts/histogram, measured mean and distribution, indexed XRD peak table, lattice parameters, refinements, atom coordinates/CIF, defect or facet determination. 4.8nm remains an author band-gap-derived estimate; hexagonal wurtzite is an author powder-diffraction assignment, not a refined atomistic model.

G8 (recognition assays): Buffer/electrolyte composition, volumes, incubation times, temperature, dye labeling ratio, exact sample dilution lineage, background corrections, repeats/errors, QY/FRET efficiency and detection limit. Preserve original arbitrary intensity plots and printed concentration labels without inventing calibration or protein-count-per-QD values.

G9 (SI acquisition): TEM drop/dilution/drying numbers, XRD freeze-drying/loading details, dwell/scan rate, provenance and indexing of reference sticks, separately labeled polymer-only XRD trace. No assignment of sharp XRD features to polymer/impurity and no background subtraction inferred.

G10 (external cited sources): Full primary procedures/data from references cited in this paper. Bibliography is inventoried as cited context only; full8-page coverage applies only to the supplied main and matched SI. No extra papers downloaded or opened.
conflicts: C1 — Figure2 polymer-concentration/PL trend. Source claim: Prose states that increasing block-copolymer concentration increased emission intensity along with a hypochromic shift. Visual observation: Caption assigns a=1.16,b=3.08,c=4.62×10^-4mol/L; printed a/b/c arrow orders the spectra from larger to smaller plotted amplitudes. The highest amplitude is labeled a and lowest c. Resolution: Unresolved source discrepancy. Preserve caption values, curve labels, image and prose separately; do not reverse concentrations, correct the word hypochromic, or create a monotonic concentration-to-size rule.

C2 — Figure5 varied protein concentration. Source claim: Caption calls the abscissa TexasRed-streptavidin concentration, while prose describes changing nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in inhibition experiments. Visual observation: Abscissa reads10^-5 Protein Conc.(mol/L), with filled/nonfilled symbols assigned to nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in the caption. Resolution: Do not decide which protein concentration varies or populate quantitative competitive-binding rows until separately resolved.

C3 — Figure6 proportionality and intensity scales. Source claim: Authors describe FRET peak as increasing proportionally with TexasRed-streptavidin concentration. Visual observation: Main plotted response is curved over its displayed micromolar range. Inset is approximately linear over a lower nanomolar range, and its arbitrary intensity scale differs from the main plot. Resolution: Retain as qualitative author conclusion plus original plots. No global linear model, calibration slope, exact limit of detection or cross-panel intensity normalization is extracted.

C4 — Protein name in figure axes. Source claim: Text and captions identify TexasRed-streptavidin. Visual observation: Graph labels abbreviate Tex-Avidin/Tex-Av Conc. Resolution: Use streptavidin according to explicit text/caption; retain the original graph labels and do not create an additional avidin reagent or claim equivalence of the proteins.

quality.review_scope: All five supplied main pages and all three content-matched SI pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source, canonical, reader, apparatus, component and product-context audits passed. Four source ambiguities, the incomplete biotin variant and all missing quantities remain explicit. The abstract size summary and optical-model size do not establish a TEM/XRD/biotin recipe-to-specimen join. No measured atomic coordinates are supplied.
missing_fields: G1 (pdp-preparation/acetal-block-polymer): Separate initiator reagent charges, EO-stage temperature, atmosphere, addition rates, PAMA protonating reagent, precipitation/extraction volumes and durations, yields/drying/storage. Present paper has an operational summary, not a fully reproducible upstream polymer SOP. References14a/14b are cited but their full texts were not inspected.

G2 (aldehyde-polymer/biotin-polymer): Polymer/solvent charges, neutralization endpoint, biocytin-hydrazide and NaBH4 amounts, reduction duration/temperature, exact purified biotin-polymer concentration and biotin functionality. Do not infer stoichiometry, quantitative biotin coverage, reduction conditions or yield.

G3 (all dialysis operations): Membrane/MWCO, time, water-exchange schedule, temperature, final volume/concentration, recovered yield and storage. Final material is an incompletely specified dialyzed dispersion; no invented isolated powder preparation.

G4 (CdS coprecipitation): CdCl2/Na2S solution-addition volumes and unequivocal stock-versus-final concentration basis, hydration state, pH, numerical ambient temperature, atmosphere, speed and addition rates. Do not multiply2.5mM by8mL to assert an added reagent charge or total yield;8mL is the initial polymer-solution volume.

G5 (comparison and concentration variants): Independent whole-batch records, exact workup and specimen links, replicate counts and outcomes per salt/concentration combination. Variants/photographs are not verified independent experiments or a timing sequence.

G6 (optical/structural sample links): Which Figure2 concentration supplies absorption trace d, Figure3 specimen, SI TEM or SI XRD; whether SI samples are biotin-ended. No exact recipe-to-structure, biotin-to-TEM, or structure-to-FRET join. Nominal same material is insufficient.

G7 (size and atomistic structure): TEM particle counts/histogram, measured mean and distribution, indexed XRD peak table, lattice parameters, refinements, atom coordinates/CIF, defect or facet determination. 4.8nm remains an author band-gap-derived estimate; hexagonal wurtzite is an author powder-diffraction assignment, not a refined atomistic model.

G8 (recognition assays): Buffer/electrolyte composition, volumes, incubation times, temperature, dye labeling ratio, exact sample dilution lineage, background corrections, repeats/errors, QY/FRET efficiency and detection limit. Preserve original arbitrary intensity plots and printed concentration labels without inventing calibration or protein-count-per-QD values.

G9 (SI acquisition): TEM drop/dilution/drying numbers, XRD freeze-drying/loading details, dwell/scan rate, provenance and indexing of reference sticks, separately labeled polymer-only XRD trace. No assignment of sharp XRD features to polymer/impurity and no background subtraction inferred.

G10 (external cited sources): Full primary procedures/data from references cited in this paper. Bibliography is inventoried as cited context only; full8-page coverage applies only to the supplied main and matched SI. No extra papers downloaded or opened.
conflicts: C1 — Figure2 polymer-concentration/PL trend. Source claim: Prose states that increasing block-copolymer concentration increased emission intensity along with a hypochromic shift. Visual observation: Caption assigns a=1.16,b=3.08,c=4.62×10^-4mol/L; printed a/b/c arrow orders the spectra from larger to smaller plotted amplitudes. The highest amplitude is labeled a and lowest c. Resolution: Unresolved source discrepancy. Preserve caption values, curve labels, image and prose separately; do not reverse concentrations, correct the word hypochromic, or create a monotonic concentration-to-size rule.

C2 — Figure5 varied protein concentration. Source claim: Caption calls the abscissa TexasRed-streptavidin concentration, while prose describes changing nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in inhibition experiments. Visual observation: Abscissa reads10^-5 Protein Conc.(mol/L), with filled/nonfilled symbols assigned to nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in the caption. Resolution: Do not decide which protein concentration varies or populate quantitative competitive-binding rows until separately resolved.

C3 — Figure6 proportionality and intensity scales. Source claim: Authors describe FRET peak as increasing proportionally with TexasRed-streptavidin concentration. Visual observation: Main plotted response is curved over its displayed micromolar range. Inset is approximately linear over a lower nanomolar range, and its arbitrary intensity scale differs from the main plot. Resolution: Retain as qualitative author conclusion plus original plots. No global linear model, calibration slope, exact limit of detection or cross-panel intensity normalization is extracted.

C4 — Protein name in figure axes. Source claim: Text and captions identify TexasRed-streptavidin. Visual observation: Graph labels abbreviate Tex-Avidin/Tex-Av Conc. Resolution: Use streptavidin according to explicit text/caption; retain the original graph labels and do not create an additional avidin reagent or claim equivalence of the proteins.

quality.review_scope: All five supplied main pages and all three content-matched SI pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source, canonical, reader, apparatus, component and product-context audits passed. Four source ambiguities, the incomplete biotin variant and all missing quantities remain explicit. The abstract size summary and optical-model size do not establish a TEM/XRD/biotin recipe-to-specimen join. No measured atomic coordinates are supplied.
missing_fields: G1 (pdp-preparation/acetal-block-polymer): Separate initiator reagent charges, EO-stage temperature, atmosphere, addition rates, PAMA protonating reagent, precipitation/extraction volumes and durations, yields/drying/storage. Present paper has an operational summary, not a fully reproducible upstream polymer SOP. References14a/14b are cited but their full texts were not inspected.

G2 (aldehyde-polymer/biotin-polymer): Polymer/solvent charges, neutralization endpoint, biocytin-hydrazide and NaBH4 amounts, reduction duration/temperature, exact purified biotin-polymer concentration and biotin functionality. Do not infer stoichiometry, quantitative biotin coverage, reduction conditions or yield.

G3 (all dialysis operations): Membrane/MWCO, time, water-exchange schedule, temperature, final volume/concentration, recovered yield and storage. Final material is an incompletely specified dialyzed dispersion; no invented isolated powder preparation.

G4 (CdS coprecipitation): CdCl2/Na2S solution-addition volumes and unequivocal stock-versus-final concentration basis, hydration state, pH, numerical ambient temperature, atmosphere, speed and addition rates. Do not multiply2.5mM by8mL to assert an added reagent charge or total yield;8mL is the initial polymer-solution volume.

G5 (comparison and concentration variants): Independent whole-batch records, exact workup and specimen links, replicate counts and outcomes per salt/concentration combination. Variants/photographs are not verified independent experiments or a timing sequence.

G6 (optical/structural sample links): Which Figure2 concentration supplies absorption trace d, Figure3 specimen, SI TEM or SI XRD; whether SI samples are biotin-ended. No exact recipe-to-structure, biotin-to-TEM, or structure-to-FRET join. Nominal same material is insufficient.

G7 (size and atomistic structure): TEM particle counts/histogram, measured mean and distribution, indexed XRD peak table, lattice parameters, refinements, atom coordinates/CIF, defect or facet determination. 4.8nm remains an author band-gap-derived estimate; hexagonal wurtzite is an author powder-diffraction assignment, not a refined atomistic model.

G8 (recognition assays): Buffer/electrolyte composition, volumes, incubation times, temperature, dye labeling ratio, exact sample dilution lineage, background corrections, repeats/errors, QY/FRET efficiency and detection limit. Preserve original arbitrary intensity plots and printed concentration labels without inventing calibration or protein-count-per-QD values.

G9 (SI acquisition): TEM drop/dilution/drying numbers, XRD freeze-drying/loading details, dwell/scan rate, provenance and indexing of reference sticks, separately labeled polymer-only XRD trace. No assignment of sharp XRD features to polymer/impurity and no background subtraction inferred.

G10 (external cited sources): Full primary procedures/data from references cited in this paper. Bibliography is inventoried as cited context only; full8-page coverage applies only to the supplied main and matched SI. No extra papers downloaded or opened.
conflicts: C1 — Figure2 polymer-concentration/PL trend. Source claim: Prose states that increasing block-copolymer concentration increased emission intensity along with a hypochromic shift. Visual observation: Caption assigns a=1.16,b=3.08,c=4.62×10^-4mol/L; printed a/b/c arrow orders the spectra from larger to smaller plotted amplitudes. The highest amplitude is labeled a and lowest c. Resolution: Unresolved source discrepancy. Preserve caption values, curve labels, image and prose separately; do not reverse concentrations, correct the word hypochromic, or create a monotonic concentration-to-size rule.

C2 — Figure5 varied protein concentration. Source claim: Caption calls the abscissa TexasRed-streptavidin concentration, while prose describes changing nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in inhibition experiments. Visual observation: Abscissa reads10^-5 Protein Conc.(mol/L), with filled/nonfilled symbols assigned to nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in the caption. Resolution: Do not decide which protein concentration varies or populate quantitative competitive-binding rows until separately resolved.

C3 — Figure6 proportionality and intensity scales. Source claim: Authors describe FRET peak as increasing proportionally with TexasRed-streptavidin concentration. Visual observation: Main plotted response is curved over its displayed micromolar range. Inset is approximately linear over a lower nanomolar range, and its arbitrary intensity scale differs from the main plot. Resolution: Retain as qualitative author conclusion plus original plots. No global linear model, calibration slope, exact limit of detection or cross-panel intensity normalization is extracted.

C4 — Protein name in figure axes. Source claim: Text and captions identify TexasRed-streptavidin. Visual observation: Graph labels abbreviate Tex-Avidin/Tex-Av Conc. Resolution: Use streptavidin according to explicit text/caption; retain the original graph labels and do not create an additional avidin reagent or claim equivalence of the proteins.

quality.review_scope: All five supplied main pages and all three content-matched SI pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source, canonical, reader, apparatus, component and product-context audits passed. Four source ambiguities, the incomplete biotin variant and all missing quantities remain explicit. The abstract size summary and optical-model size do not establish a TEM/XRD/biotin recipe-to-specimen join. No measured atomic coordinates are supplied.
missing_fields: G1 (pdp-preparation/acetal-block-polymer): Separate initiator reagent charges, EO-stage temperature, atmosphere, addition rates, PAMA protonating reagent, precipitation/extraction volumes and durations, yields/drying/storage. Present paper has an operational summary, not a fully reproducible upstream polymer SOP. References14a/14b are cited but their full texts were not inspected.

G2 (aldehyde-polymer/biotin-polymer): Polymer/solvent charges, neutralization endpoint, biocytin-hydrazide and NaBH4 amounts, reduction duration/temperature, exact purified biotin-polymer concentration and biotin functionality. Do not infer stoichiometry, quantitative biotin coverage, reduction conditions or yield.

G3 (all dialysis operations): Membrane/MWCO, time, water-exchange schedule, temperature, final volume/concentration, recovered yield and storage. Final material is an incompletely specified dialyzed dispersion; no invented isolated powder preparation.

G4 (CdS coprecipitation): CdCl2/Na2S solution-addition volumes and unequivocal stock-versus-final concentration basis, hydration state, pH, numerical ambient temperature, atmosphere, speed and addition rates. Do not multiply2.5mM by8mL to assert an added reagent charge or total yield;8mL is the initial polymer-solution volume.

G5 (comparison and concentration variants): Independent whole-batch records, exact workup and specimen links, replicate counts and outcomes per salt/concentration combination. Variants/photographs are not verified independent experiments or a timing sequence.

G6 (optical/structural sample links): Which Figure2 concentration supplies absorption trace d, Figure3 specimen, SI TEM or SI XRD; whether SI samples are biotin-ended. No exact recipe-to-structure, biotin-to-TEM, or structure-to-FRET join. Nominal same material is insufficient.

G7 (size and atomistic structure): TEM particle counts/histogram, measured mean and distribution, indexed XRD peak table, lattice parameters, refinements, atom coordinates/CIF, defect or facet determination. 4.8nm remains an author band-gap-derived estimate; hexagonal wurtzite is an author powder-diffraction assignment, not a refined atomistic model.

G8 (recognition assays): Buffer/electrolyte composition, volumes, incubation times, temperature, dye labeling ratio, exact sample dilution lineage, background corrections, repeats/errors, QY/FRET efficiency and detection limit. Preserve original arbitrary intensity plots and printed concentration labels without inventing calibration or protein-count-per-QD values.

G9 (SI acquisition): TEM drop/dilution/drying numbers, XRD freeze-drying/loading details, dwell/scan rate, provenance and indexing of reference sticks, separately labeled polymer-only XRD trace. No assignment of sharp XRD features to polymer/impurity and no background subtraction inferred.

G10 (external cited sources): Full primary procedures/data from references cited in this paper. Bibliography is inventoried as cited context only; full8-page coverage applies only to the supplied main and matched SI. No extra papers downloaded or opened.
conflicts: C1 — Figure2 polymer-concentration/PL trend. Source claim: Prose states that increasing block-copolymer concentration increased emission intensity along with a hypochromic shift. Visual observation: Caption assigns a=1.16,b=3.08,c=4.62×10^-4mol/L; printed a/b/c arrow orders the spectra from larger to smaller plotted amplitudes. The highest amplitude is labeled a and lowest c. Resolution: Unresolved source discrepancy. Preserve caption values, curve labels, image and prose separately; do not reverse concentrations, correct the word hypochromic, or create a monotonic concentration-to-size rule.

C2 — Figure5 varied protein concentration. Source claim: Caption calls the abscissa TexasRed-streptavidin concentration, while prose describes changing nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in inhibition experiments. Visual observation: Abscissa reads10^-5 Protein Conc.(mol/L), with filled/nonfilled symbols assigned to nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in the caption. Resolution: Do not decide which protein concentration varies or populate quantitative competitive-binding rows until separately resolved.

C3 — Figure6 proportionality and intensity scales. Source claim: Authors describe FRET peak as increasing proportionally with TexasRed-streptavidin concentration. Visual observation: Main plotted response is curved over its displayed micromolar range. Inset is approximately linear over a lower nanomolar range, and its arbitrary intensity scale differs from the main plot. Resolution: Retain as qualitative author conclusion plus original plots. No global linear model, calibration slope, exact limit of detection or cross-panel intensity normalization is extracted.

C4 — Protein name in figure axes. Source claim: Text and captions identify TexasRed-streptavidin. Visual observation: Graph labels abbreviate Tex-Avidin/Tex-Av Conc. Resolution: Use streptavidin according to explicit text/caption; retain the original graph labels and do not create an additional avidin reagent or claim equivalence of the proteins.

quality.review_scope: All five supplied main pages and all three content-matched SI pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source, canonical, reader, apparatus, component and product-context audits passed. Four source ambiguities, the incomplete biotin variant and all missing quantities remain explicit. The abstract size summary and optical-model size do not establish a TEM/XRD/biotin recipe-to-specimen join. No measured atomic coordinates are supplied.
missing_fields: G1 (pdp-preparation/acetal-block-polymer): Separate initiator reagent charges, EO-stage temperature, atmosphere, addition rates, PAMA protonating reagent, precipitation/extraction volumes and durations, yields/drying/storage. Present paper has an operational summary, not a fully reproducible upstream polymer SOP. References14a/14b are cited but their full texts were not inspected.

G2 (aldehyde-polymer/biotin-polymer): Polymer/solvent charges, neutralization endpoint, biocytin-hydrazide and NaBH4 amounts, reduction duration/temperature, exact purified biotin-polymer concentration and biotin functionality. Do not infer stoichiometry, quantitative biotin coverage, reduction conditions or yield.

G3 (all dialysis operations): Membrane/MWCO, time, water-exchange schedule, temperature, final volume/concentration, recovered yield and storage. Final material is an incompletely specified dialyzed dispersion; no invented isolated powder preparation.

G4 (CdS coprecipitation): CdCl2/Na2S solution-addition volumes and unequivocal stock-versus-final concentration basis, hydration state, pH, numerical ambient temperature, atmosphere, speed and addition rates. Do not multiply2.5mM by8mL to assert an added reagent charge or total yield;8mL is the initial polymer-solution volume.

G5 (comparison and concentration variants): Independent whole-batch records, exact workup and specimen links, replicate counts and outcomes per salt/concentration combination. Variants/photographs are not verified independent experiments or a timing sequence.

G6 (optical/structural sample links): Which Figure2 concentration supplies absorption trace d, Figure3 specimen, SI TEM or SI XRD; whether SI samples are biotin-ended. No exact recipe-to-structure, biotin-to-TEM, or structure-to-FRET join. Nominal same material is insufficient.

G7 (size and atomistic structure): TEM particle counts/histogram, measured mean and distribution, indexed XRD peak table, lattice parameters, refinements, atom coordinates/CIF, defect or facet determination. 4.8nm remains an author band-gap-derived estimate; hexagonal wurtzite is an author powder-diffraction assignment, not a refined atomistic model.

G8 (recognition assays): Buffer/electrolyte composition, volumes, incubation times, temperature, dye labeling ratio, exact sample dilution lineage, background corrections, repeats/errors, QY/FRET efficiency and detection limit. Preserve original arbitrary intensity plots and printed concentration labels without inventing calibration or protein-count-per-QD values.

G9 (SI acquisition): TEM drop/dilution/drying numbers, XRD freeze-drying/loading details, dwell/scan rate, provenance and indexing of reference sticks, separately labeled polymer-only XRD trace. No assignment of sharp XRD features to polymer/impurity and no background subtraction inferred.

G10 (external cited sources): Full primary procedures/data from references cited in this paper. Bibliography is inventoried as cited context only; full8-page coverage applies only to the supplied main and matched SI. No extra papers downloaded or opened.
conflicts: C1 — Figure2 polymer-concentration/PL trend. Source claim: Prose states that increasing block-copolymer concentration increased emission intensity along with a hypochromic shift. Visual observation: Caption assigns a=1.16,b=3.08,c=4.62×10^-4mol/L; printed a/b/c arrow orders the spectra from larger to smaller plotted amplitudes. The highest amplitude is labeled a and lowest c. Resolution: Unresolved source discrepancy. Preserve caption values, curve labels, image and prose separately; do not reverse concentrations, correct the word hypochromic, or create a monotonic concentration-to-size rule.

C2 — Figure5 varied protein concentration. Source claim: Caption calls the abscissa TexasRed-streptavidin concentration, while prose describes changing nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in inhibition experiments. Visual observation: Abscissa reads10^-5 Protein Conc.(mol/L), with filled/nonfilled symbols assigned to nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in the caption. Resolution: Do not decide which protein concentration varies or populate quantitative competitive-binding rows until separately resolved.

C3 — Figure6 proportionality and intensity scales. Source claim: Authors describe FRET peak as increasing proportionally with TexasRed-streptavidin concentration. Visual observation: Main plotted response is curved over its displayed micromolar range. Inset is approximately linear over a lower nanomolar range, and its arbitrary intensity scale differs from the main plot. Resolution: Retain as qualitative author conclusion plus original plots. No global linear model, calibration slope, exact limit of detection or cross-panel intensity normalization is extracted.

C4 — Protein name in figure axes. Source claim: Text and captions identify TexasRed-streptavidin. Visual observation: Graph labels abbreviate Tex-Avidin/Tex-Av Conc. Resolution: Use streptavidin according to explicit text/caption; retain the original graph labels and do not create an additional avidin reagent or claim equivalence of the proteins.

quality.review_scope: All five supplied main pages and all three content-matched SI pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source, canonical, reader, apparatus, component and product-context audits passed. Four source ambiguities, the incomplete biotin variant and all missing quantities remain explicit. The abstract size summary and optical-model size do not establish a TEM/XRD/biotin recipe-to-specimen join. No measured atomic coordinates are supplied.
missing_fields: G1 (pdp-preparation/acetal-block-polymer): Separate initiator reagent charges, EO-stage temperature, atmosphere, addition rates, PAMA protonating reagent, precipitation/extraction volumes and durations, yields/drying/storage. Present paper has an operational summary, not a fully reproducible upstream polymer SOP. References14a/14b are cited but their full texts were not inspected.

G2 (aldehyde-polymer/biotin-polymer): Polymer/solvent charges, neutralization endpoint, biocytin-hydrazide and NaBH4 amounts, reduction duration/temperature, exact purified biotin-polymer concentration and biotin functionality. Do not infer stoichiometry, quantitative biotin coverage, reduction conditions or yield.

G3 (all dialysis operations): Membrane/MWCO, time, water-exchange schedule, temperature, final volume/concentration, recovered yield and storage. Final material is an incompletely specified dialyzed dispersion; no invented isolated powder preparation.

G4 (CdS coprecipitation): CdCl2/Na2S solution-addition volumes and unequivocal stock-versus-final concentration basis, hydration state, pH, numerical ambient temperature, atmosphere, speed and addition rates. Do not multiply2.5mM by8mL to assert an added reagent charge or total yield;8mL is the initial polymer-solution volume.

G5 (comparison and concentration variants): Independent whole-batch records, exact workup and specimen links, replicate counts and outcomes per salt/concentration combination. Variants/photographs are not verified independent experiments or a timing sequence.

G6 (optical/structural sample links): Which Figure2 concentration supplies absorption trace d, Figure3 specimen, SI TEM or SI XRD; whether SI samples are biotin-ended. No exact recipe-to-structure, biotin-to-TEM, or structure-to-FRET join. Nominal same material is insufficient.

G7 (size and atomistic structure): TEM particle counts/histogram, measured mean and distribution, indexed XRD peak table, lattice parameters, refinements, atom coordinates/CIF, defect or facet determination. 4.8nm remains an author band-gap-derived estimate; hexagonal wurtzite is an author powder-diffraction assignment, not a refined atomistic model.

G8 (recognition assays): Buffer/electrolyte composition, volumes, incubation times, temperature, dye labeling ratio, exact sample dilution lineage, background corrections, repeats/errors, QY/FRET efficiency and detection limit. Preserve original arbitrary intensity plots and printed concentration labels without inventing calibration or protein-count-per-QD values.

G9 (SI acquisition): TEM drop/dilution/drying numbers, XRD freeze-drying/loading details, dwell/scan rate, provenance and indexing of reference sticks, separately labeled polymer-only XRD trace. No assignment of sharp XRD features to polymer/impurity and no background subtraction inferred.

G10 (external cited sources): Full primary procedures/data from references cited in this paper. Bibliography is inventoried as cited context only; full8-page coverage applies only to the supplied main and matched SI. No extra papers downloaded or opened.
conflicts: C1 — Figure2 polymer-concentration/PL trend. Source claim: Prose states that increasing block-copolymer concentration increased emission intensity along with a hypochromic shift. Visual observation: Caption assigns a=1.16,b=3.08,c=4.62×10^-4mol/L; printed a/b/c arrow orders the spectra from larger to smaller plotted amplitudes. The highest amplitude is labeled a and lowest c. Resolution: Unresolved source discrepancy. Preserve caption values, curve labels, image and prose separately; do not reverse concentrations, correct the word hypochromic, or create a monotonic concentration-to-size rule.

C2 — Figure5 varied protein concentration. Source claim: Caption calls the abscissa TexasRed-streptavidin concentration, while prose describes changing nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in inhibition experiments. Visual observation: Abscissa reads10^-5 Protein Conc.(mol/L), with filled/nonfilled symbols assigned to nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in the caption. Resolution: Do not decide which protein concentration varies or populate quantitative competitive-binding rows until separately resolved.

C3 — Figure6 proportionality and intensity scales. Source claim: Authors describe FRET peak as increasing proportionally with TexasRed-streptavidin concentration. Visual observation: Main plotted response is curved over its displayed micromolar range. Inset is approximately linear over a lower nanomolar range, and its arbitrary intensity scale differs from the main plot. Resolution: Retain as qualitative author conclusion plus original plots. No global linear model, calibration slope, exact limit of detection or cross-panel intensity normalization is extracted.

C4 — Protein name in figure axes. Source claim: Text and captions identify TexasRed-streptavidin. Visual observation: Graph labels abbreviate Tex-Avidin/Tex-Av Conc. Resolution: Use streptavidin according to explicit text/caption; retain the original graph labels and do not create an additional avidin reagent or claim equivalence of the proteins.

missing_fields: G1 (pdp-preparation/acetal-block-polymer): Separate initiator reagent charges, EO-stage temperature, atmosphere, addition rates, PAMA protonating reagent, precipitation/extraction volumes and durations, yields/drying/storage. Present paper has an operational summary, not a fully reproducible upstream polymer SOP. References14a/14b are cited but their full texts were not inspected.

G2 (aldehyde-polymer/biotin-polymer): Polymer/solvent charges, neutralization endpoint, biocytin-hydrazide and NaBH4 amounts, reduction duration/temperature, exact purified biotin-polymer concentration and biotin functionality. Do not infer stoichiometry, quantitative biotin coverage, reduction conditions or yield.

G3 (all dialysis operations): Membrane/MWCO, time, water-exchange schedule, temperature, final volume/concentration, recovered yield and storage. Final material is an incompletely specified dialyzed dispersion; no invented isolated powder preparation.

G4 (CdS coprecipitation): CdCl2/Na2S solution-addition volumes and unequivocal stock-versus-final concentration basis, hydration state, pH, numerical ambient temperature, atmosphere, speed and addition rates. Do not multiply2.5mM by8mL to assert an added reagent charge or total yield;8mL is the initial polymer-solution volume.

G5 (comparison and concentration variants): Independent whole-batch records, exact workup and specimen links, replicate counts and outcomes per salt/concentration combination. Variants/photographs are not verified independent experiments or a timing sequence.

G6 (optical/structural sample links): Which Figure2 concentration supplies absorption trace d, Figure3 specimen, SI TEM or SI XRD; whether SI samples are biotin-ended. No exact recipe-to-structure, biotin-to-TEM, or structure-to-FRET join. Nominal same material is insufficient.

G7 (size and atomistic structure): TEM particle counts/histogram, measured mean and distribution, indexed XRD peak table, lattice parameters, refinements, atom coordinates/CIF, defect or facet determination. 4.8nm remains an author band-gap-derived estimate; hexagonal wurtzite is an author powder-diffraction assignment, not a refined atomistic model.

G8 (recognition assays): Buffer/electrolyte composition, volumes, incubation times, temperature, dye labeling ratio, exact sample dilution lineage, background corrections, repeats/errors, QY/FRET efficiency and detection limit. Preserve original arbitrary intensity plots and printed concentration labels without inventing calibration or protein-count-per-QD values.

G9 (SI acquisition): TEM drop/dilution/drying numbers, XRD freeze-drying/loading details, dwell/scan rate, provenance and indexing of reference sticks, separately labeled polymer-only XRD trace. No assignment of sharp XRD features to polymer/impurity and no background subtraction inferred.

G10 (external cited sources): Full primary procedures/data from references cited in this paper. Bibliography is inventoried as cited context only; full8-page coverage applies only to the supplied main and matched SI. No extra papers downloaded or opened.
conflicts: C1 — Figure2 polymer-concentration/PL trend. Source claim: Prose states that increasing block-copolymer concentration increased emission intensity along with a hypochromic shift. Visual observation: Caption assigns a=1.16,b=3.08,c=4.62×10^-4mol/L; printed a/b/c arrow orders the spectra from larger to smaller plotted amplitudes. The highest amplitude is labeled a and lowest c. Resolution: Unresolved source discrepancy. Preserve caption values, curve labels, image and prose separately; do not reverse concentrations, correct the word hypochromic, or create a monotonic concentration-to-size rule.

C2 — Figure5 varied protein concentration. Source claim: Caption calls the abscissa TexasRed-streptavidin concentration, while prose describes changing nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in inhibition experiments. Visual observation: Abscissa reads10^-5 Protein Conc.(mol/L), with filled/nonfilled symbols assigned to nonlabeled streptavidin/BSA in the caption. Resolution: Do not decide which protein concentration varies or populate quantitative competitive-binding rows until separately resolved.

C3 — Figure6 proportionality and intensity scales. Source claim: Authors describe FRET peak as increasing proportionally with TexasRed-streptavidin concentration. Visual observation: Main plotted response is curved over its displayed micromolar range. Inset is approximately linear over a lower nanomolar range, and its arbitrary intensity scale differs from the main plot. Resolution: Retain as qualitative author conclusion plus original plots. No global linear model, calibration slope, exact limit of detection or cross-panel intensity normalization is extracted.

C4 — Protein name in figure axes. Source claim: Text and captions identify TexasRed-streptavidin. Visual observation: Graph labels abbreviate Tex-Avidin/Tex-Av Conc. Resolution: Use streptavidin according to explicit text/caption; retain the original graph labels and do not create an additional avidin reagent or claim equivalence of the proteins.

missing_fields: Preparation, quantitative carrier-solvent composition and purity of the supplied 2 M TOP-S stock.
Exact physical parent CdSe-core batch, seed dispersion volume/carrier and core storage conditions.
Reagent suppliers, purities/lots, flask capacity, stirring, heating rate, gas-flow rate and pressure.
Duration to CdO dissolution, numeric injection duration, post-injection temperature trajectory, final bulk hold endpoint and quench.
Aliquot masses/volumes; the generic TEM workup sampling time; initial ethanol precipitation amount.
Individual centrifugation durations, detailed fraction transfers, final bulk isolation/redispersion and storage.
Original Cirillo et al. 2014 flash method is cited but not independently reviewed in this bounded audit.
Low-acid absolute OA charge and definition of free-versus-total acid ratio.
Exact physical batch identity for the low-OA Figure 1d-f series, its TEM specimen, and any diffraction specimen; no low-OA size or shell-thickness statistic is reported.
conflicts: The parent high-OA method lists 5.6 mmol OA/0.25 mmol CdO (22.4 charged ratio), whereas its results use 20:1. The low-OA branch is labeled 3:1, but the free-versus-total acid basis and absolute low-OA charge are unresolved. No high-OA charge or 8.6 nm size is assigned to this branch.

quality.review_scope: All twelve supplied main pages and all four content-matched SI pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source, canonical, reader and private visual audits passed. Absolute recipe scale and multiple workup conditions remain unreported. Keep the 0.02% feed EPR series, 0.20 +/- 0.01% measured colloids, 1.1% TOPO/MCD specimen and optical/model contexts separate. An external undoped ZnO cell is a reference, not measured Mn:ZnO coordinates.
missing_fields: g-absolute-scale (Absolute recipe scale): No absolute reagent masses, stock/reaction volumes, yield, addition rate, wash volumes/cycle counts, separation force/time, or quantified initial capping stage are supplied. Retain partial protocols; do not call these fully quantified recipes or complete laboratory SOPs.

g-tmah-formula (TMAH formula discrepancy): Materials prints N(CH4)4OH·5H2O, whereas sample preparation prints N(Me)4OH·5H2O. Normalize the named tetramethylammonium identity while retaining the printed discrepancy.
g-base (Base amount and clouding): The titration begins to cloud beyond ca. 1.65 equivalents, while the common preparation uses 1.7 equivalents. Preserve the separate experimental scopes.

g-topo (TOPO route): The alternative procedure cites reference 32 without restating its full conditions. That referenced full paper was not inspected for this extraction. Keep the alternative partial; do not inherit the dodecylamine treatment conditions.

g-mn-feed (Feed and measured dopant content): Only the 0.20±0.01% product is explicitly linked to a 0.50% feed. The EPR series uses a 0.02% feed/nominal label; optical and MCD samples do not supply their initial feed. Retain separate sample identities and mask unavailable feed/outcome fields.
g-s4-count (SI table count): The main article announces three SI tables; the matched supplied SI contains four. Inventory all four, including the six-film Table S4.

g-poisson (SI statistical notation): The printed variables and λ definition mix concentration with mean dopants per particle. The reported means are 7.9 and 79, not fractions 0.0013 and 0.013. Preserve the equations, original figure and author-reported means as a model with a notation gap; do not silently repair it.

g-structure (Atomic structure and SAED): Wurtzite is supported by XRD and HRTEM. No experimental CIF, atomic coordinates, refined site occupancies, numerical lattice constants, or SAED pattern appear in the inspected main/SI. Allow phase/morphology evidence; exclude an exact experimental atomic-structure/recipe label.

g-film-df (Films D–F preparation): The SI gives film masses and magnetization, but omits coat counts, individual parent batches, and independently stated annealing conditions. Retain partial outcomes; do not assign 20 or 40 coats by proximity.

g-si-curve-table (Figure S3 / Table S4 conflict): Figure S3b visually orders mass-normalized high-field curves D > E > F, whereas Table S4 lists D = 0.038, E = 0.059, F = 0.076 emu/g. quality.review_scope: All twelve supplied main pages and all four content-matched SI pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source, canonical, reader and private visual audits passed. Absolute recipe scale and multiple workup conditions remain unreported. Keep the 0.02% feed EPR series, 0.20 +/- 0.01% measured colloids, 1.1% TOPO/MCD specimen and optical/model contexts separate. Preserve SI statistical-notation and Figure S3/Table S4 D/F conflicts. Films A-C preparation does not supply missing D-F coat counts or annealing conditions. An external undoped ZnO cell is a reference, not measured Mn:ZnO coordinates.
missing_fields: g-absolute-scale (Absolute recipe scale): No absolute reagent masses, stock/reaction volumes, yield, addition rate, wash volumes/cycle counts, separation force/time, or quantified initial capping stage are supplied. Retain partial protocols; do not call these fully quantified recipes or complete laboratory SOPs.

g-tmah-formula (TMAH formula discrepancy): Materials prints N(CH4)4OH·5H2O, whereas sample preparation prints N(Me)4OH·5H2O. Normalize the named tetramethylammonium identity while retaining the printed discrepancy.
g-base (Base amount and clouding): The titration begins to cloud beyond ca. 1.65 equivalents, while the common preparation uses 1.7 equivalents. Preserve the separate experimental scopes.

g-topo (TOPO route): The alternative procedure cites reference 32 without restating its full conditions. That referenced full paper was not inspected for this extraction. Keep the alternative partial; do not inherit the dodecylamine treatment conditions.

g-mn-feed (Feed and measured dopant content): Only the 0.20±0.01% product is explicitly linked to a 0.50% feed. The EPR series uses a 0.02% feed/nominal label; optical and MCD samples do not supply their initial feed. Retain separate sample identities and mask unavailable feed/outcome fields.
g-s4-count (SI table count): The main article announces three SI tables; the matched supplied SI contains four. Inventory all four, including the six-film Table S4.

g-poisson (SI statistical notation): The printed variables and λ definition mix concentration with mean dopants per particle. The reported means are 7.9 and 79, not fractions 0.0013 and 0.013. Preserve the equations, original figure and author-reported means as a model with a notation gap; do not silently repair it.

g-structure (Atomic structure and SAED): Wurtzite is supported by XRD and HRTEM. No experimental CIF, atomic coordinates, refined site occupancies, numerical lattice constants, or SAED pattern appear in the inspected main/SI. Allow phase/morphology evidence; exclude an exact experimental atomic-structure/recipe label.

g-film-df (Films D–F preparation): The SI gives film masses and magnetization, but omits coat counts, individual parent batches, and independently stated annealing conditions. Retain partial outcomes; do not assign 20 or 40 coats by proximity.
g-film-mass (Film masses): Main-text A–C masses are 0.59/0.24/0.28 mg; SI values are 593/236/279 μg. Both are retained as source reporting, consistent with rounding rather than separate replicates.

g-si-curve-table (Figure S3 / Table S4 conflict): Figure S3b visually orders mass-normalized high-field curves D > E > F, whereas Table S4 lists D = 0.038, E = 0.059, F = 0.076 emu/g. D/F identities or values are inconsistent between representations. Preserve the figure and table separately. Do not swap labels or assign resolved D/F outcome training targets. Independent audit must assess this conflict.

g-raw-curves (Raw plot data): Numerical curves and histogram counts were not supplied as raw arrays and have not been digitized. Readable original plots plus explicit scalar results are retained; do not claim raw-data recovery.

g-interpretation (Mechanistic evidence): Measured pH, carrier polarity/density, nitrogen content, and a quantitative impurity-detection limit are absent. Keep mechanistic hypotheses separate from measurements. Tc >350 K remains a lower bound.

g-other-techniques (Other characterization): No Raman, SAED, sample-specific DFT calculation, refined atomic structure, or electrical carrier-transport measurement is reported in these 16 pages. The actual additional property techniques are MCD, EPR and magnetometry; do not invent missing techniques.
